thesis: JPM sits just 2.82% below its 52-week high, but the news flow behind this run-up is diffuse rather than a single confirmed company event: a pending Fed GSIB capital-surcharge rule dispute with peers, a JPM-led AI/cybersecurity industry alliance, exploratory stablecoin plans, and broad financial-sector strength amid elevated rate expectations. No single disclosed catalyst explains the move to a near-high level, which reads as sector-wide/technical strength rather than a company-specific development.
invalidation: A break below recent support, an adverse resolution of the GSIB capital-surcharge dispute relative to peers, or a broader financial-sector reversal would undercut this setup.

thesis: CVX is up 19.31% over the past 60 days, but the move is substantially explained by a sector-wide oil-price surge tied to the escalating US-Iran conflict (Brent near $90/bbl on renewed strikes) rather than a purely company-specific event -- CVX led blue chips higher today alongside broad energy-sector gains. There are company-specific tailwinds too (a strong Q2 earnings beat, $12B vs $2.4B prior year, and CVX's position as a likely lead beneficiary of a pending, not-yet-finalized 25-year US-Venezuela oil development deal), but these are layered on top of, not clearly dominant over, the macro oil-price driver.
invalidation: A de-escalation of the Iran conflict or pullback in oil prices, or the Venezuela deal stalling/facing successful legal challenge, would remove the primary tailwind behind the rally.
